title: The pie
summary: The canteen does you a steak pie on a Friday because there's nothing else left, and you score twice on the Saturday. Now you need the pie. Every Friday. A season on, she's off sick on a Friday.

ends.title: The pie
ends.text: You've had the same steak pie every Friday for two seasons. You don't believe in it. You're not stopping.

ends.title: No pie
ends.text: You had the lucky pie for a season, then the woman from the canteen was off sick one Friday, and you scored anyway. You never had the pie again.

beats.title: Steak pie

event.title: Steak pie
event.speaker: canteen
setup: Friday. You're last to the canteen. {canteen.name} has one steak pie left. "That or nothing." You have the pie. On Saturday you score twice.

say: The next Friday, before you've said anything: "I've done you one. With your name on." It's a pie with your initials in pastry on the lid.

pie.text: You eat it. You score on Saturday. She doesn't say anything, but there's a pie with your initials on the next Friday, and the next.

salad.text: "Suit yourself." She eats the pie herself, in front of you.

two.text: "One. You'll be sick." One. You score. Two pies would have been a hat-trick, the lads reckon.

beats.hint: The canteen has one thing left

beats.title: No pie

event.title: No pie
event.speaker: canteen
setup: A season on. Friday, and {canteen.short} is off sick. The relief cook has never heard of the pie. There's a quiche.

outcomes.text: She's in bed with flu. At half nine that night her husband knocks on your door with a pie in a tea towel. Your initials. You score on Saturday.
"Pie? Eat the quiche, love." You eat the quiche.
You score on Saturday anyway. You tell her on Monday. She looks a bit put out, and makes you a pie anyway.
You eat the quiche. You score. You never have the pie again, and she pretends not to mind.

beats.hint: A season on, a Friday without her
